diogo-sousa.name: D. Diogo de Sousa Archaeology Museum
diogo-sousa.short: The archaeology museum of Roman Bracara Augusta, from the Palaeolithic to the Middle Ages
diogo-sousa.long: The museum was founded in 1918 but got a building of its own only in 2007. The architects Carlos Guimarães and Luís Soares Carneiro placed it in the most important archaeological zone of Roman Bracara Augusta. The collection covers northern Portugal from the Palaeolithic to the Middle Ages. It holds one of Europe’s finest collections of Roman milestones.
diogo-sousa.history:
The museum is named after Diogo de Sousa (1461–1532), Archbishop of Braga from 1505. He remodelled the city and was among the first to protect the heritage of Roman Bracara Augusta. The archbishop gathered Roman milestones and set them up on the Campo de Sant’Ana, today’s Avenida Central, creating the city’s first open-air “museum”. In 1769 Archbishop Gaspar de Bragança moved the stones to the Alameda das Carvalheiras.

The town council decided to create a museum as early as 1892, but the decision stayed on paper. The museum was officially founded by a decree of 28 March 1918 as a museum of archaeology and art. It occupied rooms in the Archbishop’s Palace but did not work regularly until 1980. That year it was revived as the Regional Archaeology Museum.

Work on a new building began around 1990. It soon stalled: the new heads of the museum service called the project a “white elephant”. Work resumed in 2001, and the museum opened on 29 June 2007. The design is by Carlos Guimarães and Luís Soares Carneiro, architects of the Porto School. The building has three wings: a technical wing with a conservation laboratory, a café, and a public wing with galleries, an auditorium, a library and a shop. The gardens around it are open to all.

The collection holds more than 30,000 objects. The Roman milestones of the Capela inventory have been a National Monument since 1910. One Roman mosaic floor is shown where it was found. In 2018–2019 the German patrons Bühler-Brockhaus donated almost 300 ancient objects. Among them is a bust of Emperor Augustus made in his lifetime, the only one in Portugal.

diogo-sousa.tip: The museum is open Tuesday to Sunday, 10:00–17:30, and a full ticket costs €5. The gardens around the building are free. The Roman baths on the Alto da Cividade are close by.
